title: SSK: left-leaning decrease
subtitle: The mirror of k2tog, leaning the decrease to the left.
excerpt: SSK (slip, slip, knit) creates a left-leaning decrease by slipping two stitches knitwise and knitting through their back loops together. The UK equivalent is sl1, k1, psso.
sourceNotes: Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), decreases chapter. UK equivalent sl1-k1-psso documented in Weldon's Practical Knitter (1886).

glossaryTerms.definition: Slip, slip, knit: a left-leaning single decrease worked by slipping two stitches knitwise one at a time, then inserting the left needle through both slipped stitches from left to right and knitting them together. UK patterns sometimes write sl1, k1, psso (slip 1, knit 1, pass slipped stitch over) for a similar result.
Inserting the needle into a stitch from left to right (as if to knit) and slipping it to the right needle without working it. This re-orients the stitch's leading leg.

content.text: SSK (slip, slip, knit) is the standard left-leaning decrease. UK pattern books often write the same move as 'sl1, k1, psso' (slip one knitwise, knit one, pass slipped stitch over), which achieves a near-identical lean but leaves a slightly different texture. The SSK version is now more common because it produces a cleaner lean that mirrors k2tog precisely.
and k2tog are worked in pairs on every decrease row in lace and on hat crowns, sock toes, and raglan seams. Difficulty: beginner.
DK yarn and 4 mm needles with a few rows worked
Work to the position where the decrease is needed.
(insert the right needle as if to knit, then slip the stitch without working it).
Slip the second stitch knitwise in the same way.
Insert the left needle tip through the front of both slipped stitches from left to right.
Knit both stitches together by wrapping the yarn around the right needle and drawing a loop through both. Slip both stitches off the left needle.

SSK appears on the left side of every symmetrically shaped knitted piece: the left side of a lace motif, the left end of a sock toe, the left side of a raglan increase line. When a lace chart shows a left-leaning symbol, it is almost always SSK. UK vintage patterns may write sl1-k1-psso; the lean and appearance are similar enough that the two can be substituted.

items.symptom: SSK still looks as if it leans right
items.cause: One or both stitches slipped purlwise instead of knitwise
items.fix: Both slips must be knitwise (needle enters from the left). If either slip is purlwise, the stitch is not re-oriented and the resulting decrease looks twisted.

items.cause: SSK naturally leaves a slightly looser stitch in most yarns
items.fix: Give the yarn a small tug after completing the SSK to snug it. Some knitters prefer to work the SSK slightly tighter than the adjacent stitches to compensate.
